subject: Follow-up: FinTechCo deployment controls (Dedicated vs Private VPC)
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@fintechco.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: FinTechCo deployment controls (Dedicated vs Private VPC)

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. I copied Karthik (AE) and Ben (SE) for follow-up.

Call summary (high level)
- FinTechCo is evaluating Redwood for customer-facing decisioning and document processing.
- Primary concern: data custody and logical/physical isolation for PCI & PII workloads.
- Shortlist: Dedicated GPU capacity (Redwood Dedicated) vs Private VPC/on-prem (Redwood Private). Hosted API ruled out for scope due to regulatory constraints.

Key requirements you raised
- Customer-managed encryption keys (BYOK/KMS) so keys never held by vendor.
- Network-level isolation: model and inference traffic must remain within customer VPC or on-prem network; no egress to shared control plane without explicit authorization.
- Auditability: request-level logs (request id, model version, latency) retained for 7 years and exportable to your SIEM.
- Change management: any model updates/patches must be coordinated; you prefer a scheduled patch window and advance notice.

Open qualification items (actionable)
1) Confirm whether "keys must never leave customer network" means: a) customer KMS with HSM on their cloud account + control-plane routing via private link, OR b) fully air-gapped on-prem HSM.
2) Is there a requirement for running inference on customer-managed hardware (no vendor-managed GPUs)?
3) Who (title) on FinTechCo will be the infra owner for a security checklist review? We proposed network/security and compliance folks.

Attachments: RDW_Dedicated_vs_VPC_Matrix.pdf — short matrix of tradeoffs (latency, ops, control plane reachability, KMS options).

Next steps
- Ben to respond with technical details on KMS/HSM options and control-plane access.
- If Private VPC looks required, propose a technical deep-dive with your infra team next week (30–45 min).
- Please confirm answers to the three qualification items above so we can scope an internal cost/ops estimate.

Thanks — happy to adjust if I missed anything.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Sales | Redwood Inference
[jasmine.liu@redwood.ai] | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@fintechco.com>

Cc: Luis Gomez <luis.gomez@fintechco.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Mar 2028 09:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Follow-up: FinTechCo deployment controls (Dedicated vs Private VPC)

Thanks Jasmine — this looks right. A few clarifications from our side:

- The key requirement is that customer encryption keys are under our control. Prefer BYOK where keys live in our cloud KMS (AWS KMS w/ HSM or Google Cloud KMS with CMEK). We are not yet committed to fully air-gapped on-prem, but need to confirm the option exists.
- We do want the inference traffic and any model artifacts (KV cache/dumped artifacts) to remain within our VPC. Control-plane calls that read low-sensitivity metadata are OK over private link, but no plaintext data should traverse vendor-managed shared networks.
- Audit logs: we need request-level logs for 7 years and an export path to our Splunk instance. Can Redwood push logs to a customer-owned S3/GCS and rotate with lifecycle policies?
- Change mgmt: correct — scheduled windows, advance notice of model updates, and ability to pin model versions per environment are required.

Two additional asks:
1) Provide evidence or pointer to prior deployments where Redwood ran in a Private VPC with customer KMS (some short case notes or architecture diagram).
2) Can you confirm whether model weights/updates are pushed by Redwood in Private deployments or if we must pull updates from a signed artifact repository? Our security team prefers pull from customer-controlled repo.

We are leaning toward Private VPC but will finalize after the technical deep dive. Proposed owners: myself (Security PM) and Luis (Cloud Infra).

Elena
Elena Morales
Security Program Manager, FinTechCo
elena.morales@fintechco.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@fintechco.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Mar 2028 11:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: FinTechCo deployment controls (Dedicated vs Private VPC)

Elena — great questions. I pulled together answers to your two asks plus a few operational notes. Attaching a short ops checklist for Private VPC.

Quick answers:
- BYOK/KMS: Supported. We can integrate with customer-managed cloud KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure) via a private-link-backed control plane integration. Keys remain in your account; Redwood will request short-lived encryption tokens scoped to a specific project. For HSM-level guarantees we support AWS CloudHSM integration or customer HSMs in on-prem footprints.

- Network egress & artifacts: In Private VPC mode, inference workloads and model caches stay in your network. No model KV cache or request payloads are mirrored to shared vendor storage. Control-plane (management API) calls can be configured to use a private endpoint; we do not require public egress for normal operation.

- Logs export: Yes — we can ship structured request logs to a customer-owned S3/GCS bucket (encrypted with your KMS) and optionally stream to your Splunk via a forwarding Lambda/Cloud Function. Retention policies are controlled by your lifecycle rules; Redwood can provide guidance on formatting and envelopes.

- Model updates/patches: Two supported patterns: (A) Redwood pushes signed model artifacts via a private artifact service into your registry over a private link (requires explicit ops agreement), or (B) customer pulls signed artifacts from Redwood's artifact repository (recommended when customers require full inbound-control). Option B is compatible with your security preference.

Operational caveats: Private VPC/on-prem requires a short onboarding window (2–4 weeks) to configure networking, KMS, and the private control plane. We provide a runbook and perform a read-only dry-run before any production cutover.

Attachment: Private_VPC_ops_checklist.xlsx [attachment]

If helpful I can prepare a small architecture diagram showing the AWS KMS + private link pattern — happy to include in the deep-dive.

—Ben
